name: STM8S207MBT6B
title: STM8S207xx/STM8S208xx performance line 24 MHz 8-bit MCU, up to 128 Kbytes Flash, data EEPROM, 10-bit ADC, timers, two UARTs, SPI, I2C, beCAN
summary: STM8S207xx and STM8S208xx are 8-bit microcontrollers on the STM8 core at up to 24 MHz (20 MIPS), with 32 to 128 Kbytes of Flash, 1 to 2 Kbytes of true data EEPROM and 6 Kbytes of RAM, running from 2.95 V to 5.5 V through an internal 1.8 V regulator that needs an external capacitor on VCAP. They carry an advanced 16-bit timer, two 16-bit general purpose timers, an 8-bit timer, a 10-bit ADC with up to 16 channels, UART1, UART3 with LIN, SPI, I2C and, on STM8S208 only, a beCAN 2.0B controller. Packages are LQFP80, LQFP64 (two sizes), LQFP48, LQFP44 and LQFP32. STM8S207MBT6B is the 128-Kbyte STM8S207 in LQFP80 14 x 14 mm (0.65 mm pitch) for -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: STM8, up to 24 MHz, 20 MIPS at 24 MHz; 0 wait states up to 16 MHz
32, 64 or 128 Kbytes; 10 k cycles, 20 years at 55 °C
8.1 mA typ, 13.2 mA max at 16 MHz HSI from Flash, 5 V
6.5 µA typ at 5 V, Flash powered down
1-24 MHz crystal or external clock, 16 MHz HSI (±1 % trimmed), 128 kHz LSI
up to 68 (80-pin), 18 high sink; 20 mA per pin max
10 bits, up to 16 channels, 14 cycles per conversion, fADC up to 6 MHz
LQFP80, LQFP64 14 x 14, LQFP64 10 x 10, LQFP48, LQFP44, LQFP32

notes: STM8S207MBT6B: STM8S207 intermediate peripheral set (no beCAN), 80 pins, 128 Kbytes Flash, LQFP, -40 °C to 85 °C, 0.65 mm pitch (LQFP80 14 x 14 mm), tray or tube.

operation.text: STM8S207xx and STM8S208xx are the high-density members of the STM8S performance line: 32, 64 or 128 Kbytes of Flash, data EEPROM, internal oscillators, watchdogs and brown-out reset on one chip for 2.95 V to 5.5 V systems, with a pinout, memory map and peripheral set shared across the family. STM8S208 adds the beCAN controller; STM8S207 has none. Register detail is in reference manual RM0016, Flash programming in PM0051, SWIM and debug in UM0470, and the instruction set in PM0044.

Harvard STM8 core with a three-stage pipeline and a 32-bit program memory bus, so most instructions are fetched in one cycle. Registers: 8-bit accumulator, 16-bit X and Y index registers, 24-bit program counter (16 Mbytes linear), 16-bit stack pointer (64 K stack levels) and an 8-bit condition code register with 7 flags. 20 addressing modes, among them indexed indirect for tables anywhere in memory and stack-pointer relative for locals; 80 instructions averaging 2 bytes, with 8 x 8 multiply, 16 / 8 and 16 / 16 divide and bit manipulation. Up to 20 MIPS at 24 MHz; Flash runs with no wait state up to 16 MHz and needs one above it (WAITSTATE option byte).

A single-wire interface (SWIM, on PD1) reaches the debug module and the memories in every operating mode, at up to 145 bytes/ms. The debug module reads and writes RAM and peripheral registers on the fly, can stall the CPU to reach everything, shows CPU state through shadow registers, and offers software breakpoints on any program instruction plus two advanced breakpoints with 23 preset configurations.

Nested interrupt controller with three software priority levels and 32 hardware-prioritised vectors, plus trap and reset. Up to 37 external interrupt pins share six vectors, the top-level interrupt TLI (PD7) among them. Port interrupts, beCAN receive, SPI and I2C can wake the chip from halt; the AWU can wake it from active halt. PA1 cannot wake it.

Single-voltage Flash up to 128 Kbytes, true data EEPROM up to 2 Kbytes and an option byte area. The data EEPROM can be written while code runs from Flash. The RAM is 6 Kbytes with the stack in its top 1 Kbyte; a 2-Kbyte boot ROM holds the bootloader. Flash is rated for 10 k write/erase cycles with 20-year retention at 55 °C; data EEPROM for 300 k cycles. Programming works on 4-byte words, 128-byte blocks or single bytes; a block takes 6 ms standard or 3 ms fast.

Flash, data EEPROM and option bytes are always write-protected by the memory access security system (MASS); writing a key sequence to a control register unlocks them for in-application programming. A second area, the user boot code (UBC), starts at the bottom of program memory and is sized in 512-byte pages by the UBC option byte, set in ICP mode, from 1 Kbyte (two pages) to the whole memory. MASS keys leave the UBC locked, so it keeps the boot program, vectors, reset routine and IAP code safe while the rest of program memory is rewritten.
With read-out protection on (ROP option byte = 0xAA), Flash and data EEPROM cannot be read or written through ICP or the debug interface. Changing the ROP state erases program and data memory.

fMASTER comes from one of four sources: a 1-24 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator (HSE), an external clock up to 24 MHz on OSCIN, the 16 MHz internal RC (HSI, user-trimmable) or the 128 kHz internal RC (LSI). After reset the chip runs from HSI/8 = 2 MHz. A prescaler divides the clock for the CPU and peripherals; switching source is glitch-free and waits until the new source is ready. Each peripheral's clock can be gated off (CLK_PCKENR1/2). A configurable clock output (CCO) puts a clock on a pin.
When enabled by software, the CSS watches the HSE; if it fails, the chip switches to HSI/8 by itself and can raise an interrupt.

Wait: the CPU stops, peripherals run, any interrupt or reset wakes it. Active halt with the main regulator on: CPU and peripheral clocks stop, the AWU wakes the chip at programmed intervals, faster wake-up for more current. Active halt with the regulator off: the same with lower current and slower wake-up. Halt: clocks stopped and main regulator off, the lowest current; an external event or reset wakes it. The REGAH bit sets the regulator state in active halt and the AHALT bit whether Flash is powered down.

Two independent watchdogs, started by option byte (hardware) or by software; once running neither can be stopped short of a reset. The window watchdog resets the chip if it is not refreshed before time-out or if it is refreshed too early (counter still above the window value); at 16 MHz its time-out ranges from 75 µs to 64 ms. The independent watchdog runs from the 128 kHz LSI, so it keeps working if the main clock fails, with a time base from 60 µs to 1 s.

The auto-wakeup counter brings the chip out of active halt; it runs from the LSI or from the HSE through a prescaler (CKAWUSEL and PRSC option bits). The LSI can be routed internally to TIM3 input capture 1 to measure it. The beeper puts a 1, 2 or 4 kHz signal on the BEEP pin.

16-bit up, down or up/down counter with a 16-bit prescaler (any ratio 1 to 65536) and auto-reload; four capture/compare channels for input capture, output compare, edge- or centre-aligned PWM and one-pulse output; three complementary outputs with programmable dead time; break input forcing the outputs to a set state; encoder mode; synchronisation with external signals. Aimed at motors, lamps and half-bridge drivers.

TIM2 (three channels) and TIM3 (two channels) are 16-bit up-counters with auto-reload and a prescaler of any power of 2 from 1 to 32768, with capture/compare and PWM. TIM4 is an 8-bit auto-reload counter clocked from the CPU clock with a power-of-2 prescaler from 1 to 128 and an update interrupt only.

ADC2 is a 10-bit successive-approximation converter with up to 16 multiplexed inputs spanning 0 V to VDDA. 80- and 64-pin parts bring out separate VREF+ and VREF- pins. A conversion takes 14 ADC clocks; single and continuous modes; it can start from an external trigger pin (ADC_ETR) or TIM1 TRGO and interrupts at end of conversion. fADC is up to 4 MHz from VDDA = 3 V and up to 6 MHz from 4.5 V.

Full-duplex asynchronous UART (NRZ) up to 1 Mbit/s (fCPU/16) with a fractional baud generator that reaches standard rates from any clock, separate transmitter and receiver enables, address-bit or idle-line wake-up, parity and error interrupts. It also does synchronous master transfers with a clock output (SPI emulation, 8-bit, 1 Mbit/s at 16 MHz), smartcard emulation, IrDA SIR, single-wire half duplex and LIN master (13-bit break sent, 11-bit break detected).

Full-duplex UART up to 1 Mbit/s with the same baud generator, wake-up modes and parity, plus LIN 2.1 master and slave. In slave mode it handles the header on its own with one interrupt per valid header, resynchronises its baud rate automatically from an initial clock error of up to ±15 %, checks the sync delimiter and identifier parity, always detects 11-bit breaks and supports hot plugging.

Up to 10 Mbit/s (fMASTER/2) as master or slave; full duplex, or simplex on two lines with an optional bidirectional data line; master or slave chosen by hardware (NSS pin) or software; hardware CRC; one-byte transmit and receive buffers.

Master (clock, start and stop generation) and slave (programmable address, stop detection) with 7- and 10-bit addressing and general call, at standard (100 kHz) and fast (400 kHz) speed. Fast mode at 400 kHz needs fMASTER of 8 MHz or more. The I2C pins PE1 and PE2 are true open-drain.

CAN 2.0A and 2.0B controller up to 1 Mbit/s with time-triggered communication support: three transmit mailboxes with priority by identifier or request order, one three-message receive FIFO, six filter banks (each two 32-bit or four 16-bit filters, list or mask mode, up to 12 filters for 29-bit or 48 for 11-bit identifiers), filter match index stored with each message, SOF time stamps, a 16-bit free-running timer and the option to disable automatic retransmission.

Eight AFR option bits move some alternate functions to other pins (the remap column of the pin table and the option byte description). A remapped function leaves its default pin. A peripheral must still be enabled in its own registers for its pins to take the function; remapping leaves the GPIO features of the pins unchanged.

Option bytes set hardware features and memory protection. Each one except ROP is stored twice, plain (OPTx) and inverted (NOPTx), as a check. They are written in ICP mode through SWIM at the EEPROM addresses of the option byte table, or by the application in IAP mode; ROP can be changed only through SWIM.

After reset the boot ROM reads the bootloader option bytes at 0x487E/0x487F and the reset vector at 0x8000 to decide whether to run the bootloader (UM0560). The bootloader pulls up UART1_RX and UART3_RX while it is active and releases them before returning. Reset release to bootloader vector fetch takes up to 150 µs.

A factory-written 96-bit identifier at 0x48CD-0x48D8 (wafer X/Y position, wafer number, lot number) is different on every device and cannot be changed. It is read byte by byte; uses include serial numbers, keys combined with cryptographic code, and secure boot.

Voltages refer to VSS. Min and max hold over the worst ambient temperature, supply and frequency, and are production-tested on every device at 25 °C and at TAmax; values marked as characterization, simulation or design data are not tested, and characterization limits are mean ± 3 Σ. Typicals are at 25 °C and VDD = 5 V and are guidance only, as are the typical curves. Pin parameters are measured with 50 pF on the pin.

VDD, VDDIO and VDDA all connect to the supply, and VSS, VSSIO and VSSA to ground; the power pins may differ by 50 mV at most, as may the ground pins. The internal main regulator needs an external capacitor CEXT from VCAP to ground: 470 nF to 3300 nF, ESR at most 0.3 Ω and ESL at most 15 nH at 1 MHz, across tolerance, temperature, DC bias and frequency. The supply must rise and fall no faster than 2 µs/V. Power-on reset releases at 2.65-2.95 V and brown-out reset trips at 2.58-2.88 V with 70 mV hysteresis.
fCPU is guaranteed up to 24 MHz from 2.95 V to 5.5 V at TA -40 to 105 °C and up to 16 MHz at -40 to 125 °C. Above 16 MHz the WAITSTATE option bit must be set.

The crystal or ceramic resonator sits between OSCIN and OSCOUT with a load capacitor CL1 = CL2 = C from each pin to ground, C being about twice the crystal's load capacitance (20 pF max). Mount the resonator and capacitors as close to the pins as possible to limit distortion and start-up time. The oscillator gm (5 mA/V min) must be well above gmcrit; a resonator with low Rm cuts the oscillator current. HSECNT sets how many HSE cycles pass before the clock is used.

Every I/O can be a floating or pull-up input (30-80 kΩ) or an open-drain or push-pull output; most can raise external interrupts. 18 high-sink pins on the 80-pin package sink 20 mA. PE1 and PE2 are true open-drain: no P-channel driver, no pull-up and no clamp diode to VDD, and they tolerate 6.5 V. Each pin sinks or sources 20 mA at most; the totals are limited per VDDIO/VSSIO pin pair, and pins switching high current together should be spread between the I/O supply pins. Unused pins must be held at a fixed level. The I/Os withstand ±4 mA of injected current per pin, 20 mA in total.

NRST has an internal pull-up of 30-80 kΩ and a filter: pulses up to 75 ns are ignored, pulses of 500 ns or more reset the chip. An internal reset drives NRST low for at least 15 µs. A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground guards against parasitic resets; an external reset source on NRST must pull it below VIL max. The capacitor can be made smaller, down to 10 nF, to save charge current; if NRST also resets other devices, their reset timing has to fit the capacitor's charge and discharge time.

The analog source charges the sample capacitor (3 pF) through its own resistance RAIN and any pin capacitance CAIN; the accuracy figures hold for RAIN below 10 kΩ. The input pin has clamp diodes to VDD and ground and about ±1 µA leakage. Negative current injected into any analog pin spoils conversions on other channels; a Schottky diode from such a pin to ground prevents it.

Susceptibility is tested on samples while the chip toggles two LEDs: ESD on every pin per IEC 61000-4-2 (class 2B) and fast transient bursts through 100 pF onto VDD and VSS per IEC 61000-4-4 (class 4A); a reset restores normal operation. Robust firmware handles a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted control registers. A low level on NRST or the oscillator pins for 1 second recovers most failures during prequalification (AN1015). Emission is measured on the LQFP80 per IEC 61967-2.

Worked case: TAmax = 82 °C, IDDmax = 15 mA at 5.5 V, eight standard outputs low at 10 mA and 2 V, four high-sink outputs at 20 mA and 1.5 V, two true open-drain outputs at 20 mA and 2 V. PINT = 82.5 mW, PI/O = 160 + 80 + 120 = 360 mW, PD = 443 mW. In LQFP64 10 x 10 (46 °C/W), TJ = 82 + 20 = 102 °C, inside the suffix 6 limit of 105 °C, so a suffix 6 part will do.
